column1: # THE BYTE-FREEZE REGISTRY.  Data, not prose.  Read by tests/byte-freeze.rs.
# AGENTS.md rule 47: record the WHOLE invocation beside every hash, including
# the flags you left at their default.  A hash without its command is not a weak
# record, it is not a record at all.  The test does not merely *check* the rows
# against a command written somewhere else -- it BUILDS the command out of the
# row, so the hash and the invocation cannot drift apart, and one milestone's
# flag can never be spliced onto another milestone's command.  That splice is
# fact 1379: it cost a 1.9-hour investigation into a regression that had not
# happened.
# TAB-separated.  Blank lines and lines beginning with `#` are ignored.  The
# header row is checked verbatim, so renaming or reordering a column fails loudly
# instead of silently shifting every field one to the left.
# COLUMNS
#   id              kebab-case, unique.  Names the invocation, not the milestone.
#   stack           leaf directory under the capture library (see `capture_library`
#                   in byte-freeze.rs; $STREHL_CAPTURES overrides).
#   limit           --limit, always explicit.
#   gate            --gate, always explicit AND ALWAYS BY VALUE.  `default` is a
#                   rejected value: DEFAULT_GATE moved once already and the
#                   absence of this one flag is the whole of fact 1379.
#   srgb            yes|no -- whether --srgb is passed.
#   align           off       => STREHL_ALIGN=0, no sidecar is read or written
#                   sidecar:F => STREHL_WARPMAP=tests/data/F, nothing is written
#                   `solve` is REJECTED by the validator on purpose; see the
#                   module docs of byte-freeze.rs for why.
#   alignment_mode  what the tool must REPORT on stderr for this row.  Asserted.
#                   A silent flip of this field is exactly what M86c did.
#   sha256          uppercase hex, 64 chars.
#   bytes           expected file size.
#   workers         the chunking the baseline was measured under.  REPORTED, NOT
#                   ASSERTED -- it is a property of the measuring host (RAM and
#                   core count), and a mismatch here is the first thing to suspect
#                   when a hash moves on a machine that is not the one above.
#   baselined_at    the commit at which this row's hash was last measured.
#   baselined_on    YYYY-MM-DD.
#   why             WHY the hash is what it is, and what moved it last.  This is
#                   the column that would have prevented fact 1379.  It is checked
#                   for length and for placeholders; when you re-baseline a row,
#                   REWRITE IT.  A `why` describing the previous re-baseline is
#                   worse than an empty one.
# ADDING A ROW: freezing everything is the same as freezing nothing.  See
# docs/research/M108-freeze-test.md section 5 for what earns a row and what
# does not.

column13: NOT A NEW BASELINE -- a re-record of an existing one. This hash is the D99F5D82...76CA of SYNTHESIS fact 1323 (M95's co-siting freeze, verified by ORCH at 56bd846); M108 re-measured it at fea1a72 and it reproduces exactly, so the fourth freeze in the corpus is alive, not stale. Alignment is OFF because that is the only invocation hermetic at EVERY commit: when this was measured at fea1a72, align_cmd::load_or_solve still cached a solved sidecar into the read-only capture library (repaired at dccaea8), and align_enabled() short-circuits before any path is computed. Covers decode, focus, regulariser, gate, merge and the byte-frozen encoder of merge_cmd.rs.

column13: NEW FREEZE, nothing prior to re-baseline -- no milestone had ever frozen an aligned invocation. Exists to give the unaligned row a partner: the two differ only in registration, so which of them moves says whether a change is in the merge core or in warp application. Registration comes from a COMMITTED fixture rather than a solve, which makes the row hermetic (STREHL_WARPMAP writes nothing anywhere, merge_cmd.rs:1035) and independent of the aligner solver, whose code was in flight when this was measured. The blind spot that buys is named in docs/research/M108-freeze-test.md section 4.
